\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter07.PCPPGaps}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Acceptance-maximizing input and proof]
\lean{FABL.PCPPSystem.optimalInputProof}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p179-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b001
}
\label{FABL.PCPPSystem.optimalInputProof}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.PCPPSystem.acceptanceProbability}
Let $V$ be a PCPP system with Boolean inputs of positive length, proof length $L$, and a
finite query count. Its optimal input-proof pair is a Boolean input and a Boolean proof
of length $L$ whose acceptance probability under $V$ is maximal among all such pairs.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Maximum acceptance probability]
\lean{FABL.PCPPSystem.optimumAcceptance}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b001}
\label{FABL.PCPPSystem.optimumAcceptance}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.PCPPSystem.acceptanceProbability, FABL.PCPPSystem.optimalInputProof}
Let $V$ be a PCPP system with Boolean inputs of positive length, proof length $L$, and a
finite query count. The optimum acceptance probability is the acceptance probability of
an input-proof pair maximizing acceptance probability over all Boolean inputs and proofs
of length $L$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Acceptance bounded by optimum acceptance]
\lean{FABL.PCPPSystem.acceptanceProbability_le_optimumAcceptance}
\label{FABL.PCPPSystem.acceptanceProbability_le_optimumAcceptance}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.PCPPSystem.acceptanceProbability, FABL.PCPPSystem.optimumAcceptance}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$, the proof length, and the query count be natural numbers, and let $V$ be a PCPP
system with Boolean inputs of length $n$ and proofs of the stated length. For every
input word and every proof word, the verifier's acceptance probability is at most its
maximum acceptance probability over all such words.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Optimum acceptance is at most one]
\lean{FABL.PCPPSystem.optimumAcceptance_le_one}
\label{FABL.PCPPSystem.optimumAcceptance_le_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability_le_one, FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.PCPPSystem.optimumAcceptance}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$, the proof length, and the query count be natural numbers, and let $V$ be a PCPP
system with Boolean inputs of length $n$ and proofs of the stated length. Its maximum
acceptance probability over all input words and proof words is at most $1$.
\end{theorem}

\proofstep
  {FABL.IsPCPP}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b001}
Let $n$ be positive, let $V$ be a PCPP system with Boolean inputs of length $n$, and let
$P$ be a property of those inputs. Suppose $V$ is a PCPP for $P$ with positive rejection
rate, and no input has property $P$. Then, for every input word and every proof word,
the verifier's rejection probability is strictly greater than that rate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Circuit satisfiability]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.Satisfiable}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p188-b003}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.Satisfiable}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.acceptedProperty}
A Boolean circuit on $n$ input bits is satisfiable if there exists an input on which the
circuit accepts.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Circuit unsatisfiability]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.Unsatisfiable}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p188-b003}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.Unsatisfiable}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.acceptedProperty}
A Boolean circuit on $n$ input bits is unsatisfiable if it rejects every input.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Unsatisfiability and satisfiability]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.not_satisfiable_iff_unsatisfiable}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.not_satisfiable_iff_unsatisfiable}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.Satisfiable, FABL.BooleanCircuit.Unsatisfiable}
\difficulty{1}
For a Boolean circuit $C$, there is no input assignment on which $C$ outputs true if and
only if no input assignment is accepted by $C$.
\end{theorem}

Let $n$ be positive, let $C$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ input bits, and let $D$ be a
PCPP description for the property accepted by $C$. If $C$ accepts no input, then the
verifier's maximum acceptance probability over all input words and proof words is
strictly less than $1$ minus the rejection rate of $D$.
\end{theorem}
